judged_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:257-271 (admin-group.js.es6 actions `next`/`previous` at lines 55-75) — `findMembers()` sets `offset`/`limit`/`user_count`/`members` from `result.meta`/`result.members` inside the ajax `.then`, and `next`/`previous` mutate `group.offset` synchronously before firing a new ajax call; there is no request-sequencing token, generation counter, or `.abort()`/cancellation guard, so two `findMembers()` calls in flight (e.g., a user double-clicking "next" twice) can resolve out of order and the older response's `.then` callback will overwrite `offset`/`user_count`/`members` with stale data after the newer response already rendered — the UI can silently regress the visible page while `currentPage`/`totalPages` (computed from the now-stale `offset`) show inconsistent state versus what's on screen. Rebuttal: pagination requests are typically fast and this is a minor admin UI, but the structural absence of any ordering guard is a design gap, not an implementation detail — the same model/pattern is reused for member-list refresh after add/remove, compounding exposure. Confidence 80, severity P2.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces async pagination where `Discourse.Group#findMembers()` issues an AJAX request and, in its `.then`, unconditionally overwrites `user_count/limit/offset/members` via `setProperties(...)`. The admin controller actions `next`/`previous` synchronously mutate `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()` again. There is no sequencing/cancellation (no token, generation check, or abort) to prevent an earlier request resolving after a later one and overwriting state with stale `meta`/`members`, which can regress the rendered member list and computed `currentPage/totalPages` (derived from `offset/limit/user_count`). This race is visible from the code paths added in the diff and also applies to `addMembers`/`removeMember` which call `findMembers()` after mutations.
